articleTitle: FPGA Realization of High-Efficient Address Generator Algorithm for WiMAX Deinterleaver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Utilizing the Xilinx Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), an innovative technique and low-complexity is proposed to efficiently realize the address generation circuitry of the 2D deinterleaver used in the WiMAX trans receiver. The IEEE 802.16e standard is very difficult to realize in FPGA as the floor function associated with the execution of the steps, essential for the variation of the incoming bit stream in medium interleaver/deinterleaver. To eliminates the necessity of floor function and thereby allows low-complexity FPGA implementation is done by the simple algorithm along with its mathematical background. This approach to be novel and highly efficient when compared with conventional look-up table based approach, because the utilization of an internal multiplier of FPGA, the distribution of resources for quadrature phase-shift keying, 16-quadrature-amplitude modulation, and 64-QAM modulations along with all feasible code rates. The proposed method exhibits significant improvement in the use of FPGA resources.

articleTitle: Power Efficient Hybrid Low-Power Technique for an SRAM cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In the world of battery driven devices, semiconduc-tor memories (SRAM) plays an important role. In this work, we have designed a novel hybrid low-power technique for an SRAM cell called BB-SKDG (Body-Biased Sleep Keeper and Drain Gating) for SRAM cells in the 90nm technology node. By incorporating body biasing of three transistors (PMOS) in the pull-up network and varying the SKBD terminal voltages for three transistors (NMOS) in the pull-down network, significant reductions in power consumption during write, read, and hold operations are achieved. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial decrease in average power consumption for write and read operations by 82.1 % and 73.3%, respectively, and a 89.7% reduction in static power for hold operations. The approach shows promise for various applications, including battery- powered wireless sensors, implantable healthcare devices, and embedded computers.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Low Power Techniques in SRAM Cells at 45nm Node Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper presents Gated Vdd and MTCMOS techniques to achieve low power from the simulated static random-access memory (SRAM) cells. These techniques are implemented on 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>, 5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> and 6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> memory circuits based on CMOS logic. A significant research work is already in progress in the field of electronics embedded with memory with low power technology for system on chip (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>oC). One of the most popular memory cells is 6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> SRAM for microprocessor and micro controller architectures for low power applications. This research paper discusses CMOS based SRAM circuits and the parameters considered are power dissipation and delay. Along with 6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>, the other two memory cells (4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> and 5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>) are also simulated with modifications of the low power techniques. Delay and power dissipation are analyzed for the conventional designs and modified designs with low power methodology. Low power techniques like Gated Vdd and MTCMOS (Multi Threshold CMOS), have been instrumental in reducing the power consumption at 45nm node technology. All the designs are simulated and compared to ponder on best outcome. Comparative analysis shows that the MTCMOS based SRAM cells (specially 6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>) represent overall a better choice for reduced power dissipation and delay.

articleTitle: Power Estimation of Digital VLSI Circuits Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: For any VLSI design, accurate power estimation is significant to make it optimized. Conventional approaches for power estimation are based on some analytical models and involve simulation, which is typically computationally expensive and time-consuming depending on the level of abstraction where it is performed. As an alternative machine learning-based approaches have gained popularity due to their ability to predict power consumption with higher accuracy and speed. In this paper, we presented a comparative analysis of four best performing machine learning-based approaches for power estimation of digital circuits. The dataset of various digital circuits was prepared based on the features collected from the synthesis reports obtained by Quartus tool. The Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and R-squared values are used to compare the performance of the models. In our results the best values of R-squared and RMSE obtained are 0.99 and 0.29581 respectively.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electrochemical Properties of Fe Doped TiO2 Nanotubes for Supercapacitor Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: To obtain high power density, good capacitance, and improved energy density, the choice of substrate for supercapacitor fabrication is essential. Ti0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanotube arrays (T - NTs) are excellent semiconductor substrates due to their attractive properties such as large surface to volume ratio, chemically stable, less cost, environmental friendliness, and low toxicity. However, T-NTs alone possess low conductivity and show low specific capacitance. In the present work, F e-doped Ti0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanotubes were made using a very simple, easy, one-step electrochemical anodization process, and the performance was thoroughly characterized. Scanning electron microscopy was used to characterized the structural morphology of the nanostructure and its elemental composition was confirmed by energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. The doped substrate showed significantly enhanced electrochemical properties toward high -performance energy storage application with 38 times higher specific capacitance than that of plain T -NTs at 0.1 mA/cm2 current density. Additionally, at a power density of 0.05 m W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> the modified substrate demonstrated an excellent energy density of 2.61 μ Wh/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The superior performances of the doped nanotube were accounted due to higher conductivity and improved charge transport rate at the electrode-electrolyte interface.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Design for Complex Multiplication Using Radix-4 Booth Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel design strategy for complex-number multiplication where the real part, as well as the imaginary part, are considered as a 2-point inner-product, and those inner-products are computed by radix-4 modified Booth-encoded distributed arithmetic approach where the partial inner products are reduced by the carry-save reduction process. Reduction of area complexity is achieved by sharing of Booth encoders by the pair of inner-product units. Time complexity is reduced by avoiding the vector-merging adder, which conventionally follows the carry-save reduction of partial products. The post-layout synthesis results using Cadence Innovus with a GPDK 90nm technology library and FPGA synthesis show that the proposed complex multiplier offers significant advantages in area-delay product and energy consumption over the real-number multiplier-based reference architecture.

articleTitle: High Speed Fault Tolerant Approximate Adder for Low Power Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault-tolerant approximate adder based on a controlled incrementer module, designed to meet the demands of high-performance, area-efficient arithmetic units in modern computing systems. Three distinct designs-high accuracy Algorithm-Based Adder(ABA), high-speed low power NAND and NOR-Based Adder (NNBA), and low area XOR Based Adder (XBA)-are proposed in this paper. The architectures have been implemented using Synopsys SAED 90nm Design Vision platform. Post-implementation results reveal NNBA's superiority, showcasing a 67.3% improvement in power, 86.8% in area, and 78.4% in delay compared to the conventional counterparts. This underscores the efficiency of the proposed fault-tolerant approximate adders across key metrics.

articleTitle: Test power Optimization Using Power Gating Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: A primary challenge in contemporary VLSI circuit design is imperative to optimize circuits for low power consumption. The escalation in device scaling worsens the issue of leakage power within the circuit. Among the available remedies, power gating stands out as a highly effective solution to mitigate standby leakage currents during idle periods. The main component employed in power gating is the sleep transistor, which is a crucial component in isolating the power supply (VDD or GND) from the standard cells in a particular design. Sleep transistors, appropriately sized as pMOS or nMOS, serve as the fundamental elements for powering down designated portions of the design. The underlying concept of power gating involves strategically disconnecting power sources from standard cells, contributing to substantial reductions in leakage currents during idle states. An approach to diminish the power consumption of specific fundamental gates, CMOS Inverter, D flip-flop, and conventional4-bit, 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit linear feedback shift registers (LFSR) is implemented using conventional method, an assessmentof the leakage power is conducted employing various power gating methods. The circuits were implemented using Cadence Virtuoso Tool using gpdk180.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different LFSRs for VLSI IC Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper presents a Verilog-based design and comparative analysis of Linear Feedback Shift Registers (LFSRs) for VLSI testing. Various LFSR types, such as Galois, Bit Swapping, and Bit Reversal, were studied, including their implementations, feedback tap designs, and polynomial degrees. Using Verilog HDL and Xilinx ISE Vivado ML Standard Edition, these LFSRs were simulated and synthesized. The study embeds the LFSR unit into the tested circuit, using pseudo-random patterns to detect stuck-at-faults. Comparison criteria include test pattern quality, area, and power consumption. NIST Statistical Test Suite has been run on the generated test vectors to evaluate their randomness. The performed analysis shows that optimised design of Bit Reversal Architecture proved the most efficient when we talk about the number of clock cycles required to generate the test patterns required. With the power consumption point of view, it showed a 4 % decrease in signal power but a 17.39 % increase in logic power. The work concludes that LFSR selection should align with application needs, highlighting the significance of comparative analysis for optimal LFSR choice in specific applications.

articleTitle: Circuit Techniques for High Performance in CDDK Domino Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: The designing of digital systems requires a circuit topology that is high-speed, robust, and power-efficient. To improve performance, several domino logics structures have been proposed in the literature to address the issues such as leakage current, power consumption, charge sharing, and robustness. In this paper, methods are presented to improve the speed and/or power of Clock-Delayed Dual-Keeper (shortly called CDDK) Domino circuits. This paper focus on two aspects of improving the performance such as: (i) by providing conditional additional discharge path and (ii) using multi-threshold transistor technique. The designs and evaluations of the circuits have been conducted, performed using Cadence® Virtuoso with additional features like ADEL and ADEXL with technology library of 90nm, and the results and analysis of simulating OR gate which consists of 8-inputs showed that the CDDK circuit which is having an additional discharge path resulted in a 12% increase in speed and the CDDK circuit with Multi-Threshold CMOS transistor resulted in a 44% decrease in power when compared to conventional domino logic circuits consists of Clock-Delayed Dual Keeper.

articleTitle: Pulsed Latch Based Pipelined LFSR for Cybersecurity Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel power-efficient pulsed latch-based pipelined architecture for 16-bit and 32-bit Linear Feedback Shift Registers (LFSRs). Compared to traditional flip-flop-based implementations that use two storage elements, the pulsed latch implementation uses only one storage element. This approach reduces area and power consumption in pulsed latch-based shift registers. They occupy a lesser area than the flip-flop-based shift registers and also show reduced power consumption. Leveraging this advantage, a novel pipelined LFSR architecture is proposed that showcases a 63% reduction in power consumption, making it a compelling alternative. It also increases the linear complexity and exhibits enhanced randomness, which opens doors for applications requiring high-quality random sequences, such as cryptography and secure communication protocols. The proposed design paves the way for more efficient and robust LFSR implementation with broader real-world applications.

articleTitle: Route Critical Nets in Upper Layers to Fix Timing Issues in Block Level CTS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In this study examines how the microcontroller architectures can be designed to meet the stringent field requirements rather than whether they will arrive. It describes the transition from one to multiple cores in terms of hardware coherence and consistency across various types of shared memory. Additionally, point-to-point synchronization between the processor cores can be achieved by setting up various hardware barriers. A FPGA development board with two hard PowerPC processor cores will be used in the practical tests to demonstrate the logical progression from a single-core computer to a dual- core computer. As demonstrated by extensive benchmarking of all implemented synchronization primitives as well as best and worst-case results, the hardware solutions exhibit the anticipated superiority. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that dual-ported memory performs better than single-ported memory if the many cores use more intelligent address-sensitive locking of shared memory to take advantage of the inherent parallelism.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model of TiO2 Memristor Without Control Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Memristor has found to be the replacement for CMOS transistors in different fields of electronics and in neuromorphic computations. In this work, a simple window function for LIDM is proposed without any control parameters to introduce nonlinearities to the memristor model. The proposed window function is a combination of bi-quadratic equation and cosine function. This window function does not take current through the memristor as any of its parameter and it depends completely on the state variable. This new mathematical model for the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> memristor model can resolve the boundary effect issues and is capable of maintaining symmetrical Pinched Hysteresis Loop up to a voltage of 12V without any distortions. The operating frequency range of proposed model is 0.5Hz to 15Hz and is suitable for low frequency applications.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of 2 x1 Multiplexer Based High Performance Static and Dynamic Nanoscale Carry Select Adder for Future DSP Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This study compares the performance of the 2 x 1 multiplexer-based 4-bit static and dynamic carry select adders. The design for this circuit is based on 16nm technology and features a 0.7V power supply. A step size of 10 is employed to evaluate the circuit's performance in the operational temperature range of 27 to 107 degrees Celsius. When juxtaposed with a static adder, the dynamic adder circuit showcases a notable 61.58% increase in speed at 27°C and a substantial 60.5% enhancement at 107°C. From transitioning from 27°C to 107°C, the static adder showcases a decrease in speed of 32.9%, and the dynamic adder shows a decrease of 36.6% at the same temperature shift. When comparing the two circuits at 0.7V at 27°C, the dynamic adder shows a 1.29% increase in power consumption over the static adder circuit; however, at 107°C, this increases to 3.88%, caused by the keeper transistor size. Nevertheless, the dynamic adder exhibits a great decrease in power consumption at higher supply voltages. As the temperature escalates from 27°C to 107°C, the power consumption of the static carry select adder diminishes by 10.60%, while that of the dynamic adder experiences a reduction of 12.94 %. Hence, the dynamic carry select adder outperforms its static counterpart with fewer transistors, leading to a related power consumption, improved area efficiency, higher speed, and lower short circuit power.

articleTitle: Adaptive Leaky-Integrate-And-Fire Neuron Model Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In this paper, we've developed an analog neuromor-phic circuit based on Adaptive Leaky-Integrate & Fire (LIF) model, using SCL's 180nm CMOS technology. The utilization of the LIF model is chosen for its efficiency, requiring a minimal number of transistors for spike generation. We have also eval-uated the circuit's performance by testing it with diverse input waveforms, encompassing step, pulse, sinusoidal, and sawtooth inputs, conducted for both pre-layout and post-layout. The design is compact by eliminating the traditional usage of a comparator in the LIF model, achieves a maximum energy of 1.4pJ/spike, spike rate of 8.8MHz and an overall area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$198.5\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Dual Obfuscation Techniques for DSP Based Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: IC design companies confront enormous obstacles in their efforts to prevent adversaries from reverse engineering their products. It is highly probable that the attacker will be able to physically access the chip. Countermeasures against intrusive physical attacks are not feasible from a technical or economic standpoint in most applications. Thus, hardware obfuscation is among the best methods provided to the designer. This paper discusses the security issues that consumer electronics (CE) systems confront, with a focus on the susceptibility of system-on-chip (SoC) Digital Signal Processing (DSP) intellectual property (IP) cores. The suggested method combines functional obfuscation with an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) that is voltage-key dependent with structural obfuscation techniques, like loop unrolling followed by partitioning with a fixed key, to hide internal design. The study verifies the efficacy of this dual obfuscation strategy to prevent reverse engineering and protect DSP essential functionality by evaluating the trade-off between performance and resource consumption. This provides pertinent data that can be applied in real-world situations.

articleTitle: A Modular Multilevel Derived Converter with a Robust and Dynamic Sliding Mode Control for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper proposes a bidirectional topology based on a modular multilevel converter which allows for scalability of the design for much larger voltage levels in larger EV applications. It aims to improve the modularity and reliability without a significant impact in efficiency. The converter is paired with the sliding mode control with a comprehensive decision rule which facilitates complete dynamic control of current and voltage as the switching process occurs between buck to boost and vice versa. The sliding mode control has complete self-regulation which allows the system to behave intelligently while ensuring that there are no peak overshoots in the battery voltage or current during switching and dynamic performance is still maintained.

articleTitle: Design of Spin-FET Electrical Model for Basic Gates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In conventional CMOS technology, the spin transistor (Spin-FET) is the most promising technology for resolving power consumption, speed, and non-volatility problems. This paper briefly explains the Single Gate Spin-FET electrical model for InAs channel material with a channel length of 800 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>m, which is suitable for performing digital logic functions for the local geometry of Spin-FET. Also, the simulation results were validated by performing their transient and DC simulation for different channel lengths and various spin polarization rates of the tunnel junctions. However, an inverter and a buffer gate are built using complementary Spin-FETs in order to confirm the functionality of the local geometry model. This allows for a replication of the inverter and buffer gate's behavior.

articleTitle: VLSI Implementation of CSD Based Efficient FIR Filter for ECG Signal Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel hardware-efficient Canonical Signed Digit Finite Impulse Response Filter pipelined (CSD-FIR-P) architecture using an XOR-MUX-based adder in tree topology. In this paper hardware sharing is proposed to remove the redundant computation that leads to the minimization of logic sources. Also, from the statistical analysis presented for the HDL coder coefficient and traditional CSD coefficients, it's evident that the traditional CSD coefficient is proven efficient in hardware complexity. The proposed CSD-FIR-P filter with XOR-MUX-based adder architecture is multiplier-less and is shown to be more efficient in terms of hardware utilization, area, power, and delay than conventional methods. This proposed CSD-FIR-P architecture for filter operation is applied for the ECG de-noising process. Thus the suggested FIR filter is then implemented with hardware sharing traditional CSD coefficients through Matlab to provide an effective solution (coefficients) using Verilog HDL for VLSI, with the synthesis of ASIC (180 nm technology) and FPGA (Kintex -7 xc7k70tfbv676-1 family) done with Xilinx Vivado and Cadence Genus, respectively.

articleTitle: LR-Based Performance Evaluation of MoCs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In the recent decade, on-chip communication net-works have developed into a potent platform for tackling chal-lenging and significant computation issues. However, many applications cannot achieve high-performance communication needs due to the seamless integration of computing cores in systems-on-chip (SoCs). Subsequently, a network-on-chip (NoC) has emerged as a prominent on-chip communication infrastructure in SoCs. Performance analysis of NoC's is essential for its architectural design and is traditionally evaluated employing a simulator. How-ever, simulation-based performance evaluation is relatively slow and may take a long time with varying architectural NoC sizes. This paper presents an AI-based approach for investigating mesh-based NoC (MoC) performance over the traditional simulation-based performance evaluation. The proposed framework targets to reach two objectives- quickly and accurately evaluation of various NoC performance metrics. Simulations are performed at varying architectural setups on a set of mesh NoCs to generate the training dataset for the proposed framework. Consequently, the framework satisfactorily predicts different performance metrics. For example, network and packet latency; hop count; switch, channel, and total power consumption; and total area are in the range of 58.14-88.49 and 58.69-106.97 cycles; 6.231-6.257; 1.44-13.02, 13.73-129.06, and 25.26- 177.44 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu W;$</tex> and 1.35874 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m^{2}$</tex>, respectively while the proposed framework is applied on the 9 x 9 mesh NoC. The metrics are with 94% accuracy and predicted at very significantly less time. The LR model saves 99.45 % evaluation time resulting in the speedup of 260 x than a simulation - based method.

articleTitle: A 5GHz Gain-Bandwidth Op-Amp in 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper introduces a meticulously designed single-stage operational amplifier (op-amp) utilizing GPDK 180nm CMOS technology. Operating at a 1.8V power supply, the op-amp achieves an exceptional 5GHz Gain Bandwidth Product (GBW) when faced with a 40 fF load capacitance, catering to the demands of applications like bandpass filtering and Wi-Fi technology. Employing the gm/ld methodology, the op-amp strikes a precise balance between precision and performance, accommodating functions ranging from DC bias generation to high-speed amplification. Rigorous simulations using Cadence Virtuoso validate the op-amp's adherence to specifications, affirming its efficacy in telecommunications, computers, and consumer electronics. This research presents a versatile op-amp design poised to contribute significantly to advancing technologies in various industries, combining technical excellence with adaptability for a broad range of applications.

articleTitle: Quantum-Enhanced Deep Q Learning with Parametrized Quantum Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Quantum Computing (QC) is fastly growing to replace current computing systems for many high-performance applications. Due to the rapid increase of computational power, machine learning models based on artificial neural networks (ANN) have become highly effective. Even though classical machine learning models have been performing well, quantum computing with machine learning, i.e., Quantum Machine Learning (QML), will enhance the performance in multiple ways. Subsequently, Deep <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> learning is a prominent approach to reinforcement learning used in solving complex applications for a desired performance. But this performance can be improved using a quantum computer. This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced Deep Q Learning algorithm to see its advantages over its classical counterparts. We implement our approach using parametrized quantum circuit (PQC). The evaluation of the proposed method achieves the metrics rewards and episodes up to 500 points and 1200, respectively. The performance shows that it collects roughly four times more rewards in a given time and takes significantly fewer episodes to converge compared to the classical approach.

articleTitle: Variability in Switching Characteristics of RRAM Based 1T-1R Configuration and Memory Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM) is a promising memory device for in-memory computing applications. The variability issues due to random filament formation and rupture, filament length and position variations degrade the performance of RRAM devices. In this paper, variability analysis on the RRAM Stanford model is performed by varying certain parameters of the model and the switching characteristics are analyzed. RRAM Stanford model is an existing physics-based compact model of RRAM which includes the device-to-device and cycle-to-cycle variations for circuit simulations. The parameters of the model correspond to various factors like SET-RESET voltage, current levels, HRS/LRS slope, etc. The RRAM Stanford model in 1T-1R configuration is simulated in the Cadence circuit simulator in which the effects of variations on the switching characteristics are analyzed. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\mathrm{x}3$</tex> RRAM memory array is implemented using 1T-1R configuration and the effects of parameter variations are analyzed.

articleTitle: Performance of Well-Organized VLSI Architecture for Three Operand Binary Adder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: The adder is represented as block; the Three-operand binary adder is represented as block0, the Han-Carlson adder is represented as block1, the Carry save adder is represented as block2 & the Proposed adder is represented as block3. Block0 is a pivotal functional tool in numerous cryptography and bit generator (PRBG) techniques, particularly in implementing modular arithmetic. Regarding three-operand addition, the most commonly utilized approach is the carry-save adder (CSA). Nevertheless, the ripple-carry phase inherent in the CSA introduces a notable O(n) propagation delay. Within the three-operand addition, an alternate approach entails employing block 1. This method provides a significant decrease in critical path time. A new design has been created to perform three-operand binary addition, presenting an efficient architecture combining pre-compute bitwise addition with block2 logic. This integration yields a decreased block latency of O(log2 n), accompanied by lower power consumption and a smaller spatial footprint. The proposed design has been implemented using a commercially available 180nm CMOS technology library and validated on an FPGA device to ensure its functionality. Compared to the HCA adder, the suggested design exhibits a smaller footprint, lower power dispersion, and shorter quiescence. Additionally, in terms of area, Delay Power, and leakage Power, the proposed adder surpasses current three-operand adder techniques. The proposed adder exhibits a leakage power of 1667.9n Wand a dynamic power of 17105.504 nW.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of 10T SRAM Cell Using Dopingless Vertical Nanowire Tunnel FET with NC Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: In this manuscript the SRAM cell using IOT is proposed by the use of doping less vertical nanowire tunnel FET with NC effect NC-ED-VNW-TFET. Here the device is designed with dopingless substrate to avoid random dopant fluctuation (RDF) and expensive thermal budgeting and the doping is created by electrostatic technique. Thereafter the negative capacitance (NC) effect is introduced by using piezoelectric material to reduce the required voltage to its half level. By the use of N C effect, the device is significantly useful for low power application. After designing the device and reducing the applied voltage the SRAM is designed with this device. The performance parameters like leakage power, leakage current, read signal to noise margin (RSNM), write signal to noise margin (WSNM), read delay, write delay etc. of this circuit are been contrasted with the available data of published IOT SRAM cells. After comparison it is found that the proposed device is showing better results in comparison with the published device.

articleTitle: Impact of Clock-Gating on ALU Optimized RISC-V Microarchitectures for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Due to huge demand in the general purpose processors for the applications across industries, there is a global attempt to optimize the power consumed to make it sustainable for low power applications. The proposed work aims to provide a conclusive report on reduction in switching power of a Single Cycle and Pipelined RISC- V core with focus also on adder and the multiplier circuits with optimized power consumption. The matrix multiplication assembly code is run to measure the power consumption. With the core synthesized using Cadence Genus with the saed-90nm technology node. The average power reduction of 56.9% in the switching power is observed in Single Cycle microarchitecture and 23.4% in 5-stage pipelined RISC-V micro architecture due to application of Discrete clock-gating using the Synthesis tool - Cadence Genus.

articleTitle: Analysis of Selected Load Balancing Algorithms in Containerized Cloud Environment for Microservices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Microservice architecture has become a widely accepted solution to address the challenges, particularly scala-bility, deployment, and flexibility associated with monolithic architecture. A vital attribute of the microservices architecture is its capability to handle load balancing on a large scale. The load balancer collaborates with a scaler to distribute the workload efficiently across multiple instances. In the literature, different studies employ load-balancing algorithms for efficient microservice load balancing. These works overlook cloud-based microservice applications or focus solely on virtual machines, neglecting containers. This paper addresses these limitations by comparatively assessing selected load-balancing algorithms. The three most used algorithms, random, round-robin, and least connection, are studied on a microservice application. The extensive experiments are conducted using Elastic Container Service (ECS) of Amazon Web Service (AWS) for containerized cloud setup where each service resides in a cluster and traffic is generated through Locust. Experimental results show that throughput and response time range of 6.2-288.7 and 312.2-3375.8 ms, respectively.

articleTitle: FPGA Accelerated Convolutional Neural Network for Detection of Cardiac Arrhythmia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Electrocardiogram signals (ECG) are vital features to identify a healthy body; diagnosing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) automatically with resource constraint devices at the edge has caught a significant attention in the rapid growth of smart health-care system. The rapidly developing smart world of IoT demands for low latency, less complex, and energy efficient architectures, and their deployment in real time scenarios. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) is a trading distributed embedded platform proving parallel processing, and flexibility in re-design with its re-configurable advancements. This work demonstrates a spilt 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) performing ECG beat classification on Xilinx's ZCU 104 FPGA board. The convolution has been carried out depth-wise, and performing a channel-wise addition of the half-split feature maps, so as to minimize the resource utilization by reducing the trainable parameters. A customized FPGA IP has been generated using Vitis High Level Synthesis (HLS) tool, and is implemented on ZCU 104 FPGA for the proposed less complex light-weight model. The design has achieved an accuracy of 98.64% in software, and consumed a total power of 4.177W with a latency of 2.19E8ns in classifying arrhythmia reference to Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation-AAMI EC57 standard.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Graph Neural Network Technique for Hardware Trojan Detection at Register Transfer Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: The presence of Hardware Trojans (HTs) poses a significant risk to the integrity and security of integrated circuits (ICs), as they can compromise the functionality and reliability of electronic systems. Traditional HT detection techniques rely heavily on reference designs, which limits their applicability and effectiveness. In this paper, a golden reference-free HT detection technique using Graph Neural Network (GNN) at the Register Transfer Level (RTL) is implemented. The proposed methodology leverages the power of GNNs to capture intricate relationships among various components and signals in an RTL design. The graph-based representation enables the GNN to effectively detect anomalous patterns introduced by HTs. In the proposed work, a comprehensive dataset is generated ab-initio comprising both Trojan-free and Trojan-infected designs. It includes 422 circuits which has 262 trojan free and 160 trojan infected circuits, considered for extracting the GNN based model. The proposed model learns to distinguish between normal and Trojan-infected designs, achieving high detection accuracy. The outcome indicates that that the GNN model detects unknown HT with 100 % recall, making it feasible for practical deployment in large scale design.

articleTitle: Towards Scalability and Performance: Framework for Heterogeneous Cluster Integration in Deep Learning Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: This paper presents a streamlined approach to address the challenges of integrating heterogeneous clusters in deep learning(DL) accelerators. As the demand for scalable and high-performance computing in DL continues to grow, the proposed framework offers an easy implementation solution, ensuring efficiency without compromise. The method details core components and design principles, guiding the inclusion of heterogeneous clusters step by step. Extensive experiments show the framework's adaptability, handling diverse workloads and cluster architectures. Our exploration integrates various dataflows, dynamically selected by NN during runtime for optimal performance. Results indicate improved scalability and robustness compared to existing methods. This research provides a valuable resource for practitioners seeking efficient and accessible solutions for harnessing the power of heterogeneous clusters in DL acceleration, with implications for advancements in AI and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Efficient 32-Bit Fixed-Point Newton-Raphson Division-Based Reciprocal Computing Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: Reciprocal operations play a critical role in digital signal processing (DSP), specifically in the execution of linear equation solving and Fourier analysis. For DSP architectures to support functions like adaptive filtering, channel equalization, and spectral estimation, efficient reciprocal computation is vital. Reciprocal computations frequently employ the Newton-Raphson algorithm, which is flexible concerning both floating-point and fixed-point formats. This paper proposes a digital design architecture of the reciprocal computing unit using the Newton Raphson method, which is modeled, and implemented using Verilog HDL, and the Xilinx Vivado Tool. Enhanced accuracy and substantial reductions in error rates are successfully attained using the proposed design. The average mean error rate of roughly 0.0264 % is associated with converging values. The design uses optimized resources by decreasing the required logic elements by an average of 15.76%. The results of our study emphasize the capability of our design and methodology to improve both computational efficiency and accuracy in DSP applications.

articleTitle: About the Conference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA)
abstract: The VLSI Systems, Architecture, Technology and Applications (VLSI SATA) is an annual international conference organized by the department of Electronics and Communications Engineering of School of Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Bengaluru campus. The conference was conceived in the year 2015 to promote knowledge building, engineering education, research and development activities and networking of professionals. The objective is to spread ongoing research & development activity and identify emerging techniques and applications in VLSI domain. The conference offers a forum for researchers, academicians, and practitioners from around the world to present their research works, finding and helps professional to establish collaboration with experts. The conference was paused because of some unavoidable reasons after successful event in 2016. However, the conference started again from 2024 and become regular event. The conference is financially and technically sponsored by IEEE Circuit and System Society (CAS) Bangalore Chapter.
